comment: Frame 074, printed p. 68: the outer western and northern sea continued, in running text: the coast from point to point, with the editor's running numbers (١٠٠٣)-(١٠٢٧) and the numbers of Suhrāb, past the mouth of a river, the shape of the qawwāra and the shape of the ṭaylasān, northwards to the latitude of 71; the folio of the manuscript, «(fol. 17ᵃ)», within the line. Three lines of the editor's footnotes.

variants: L03: a variant reading of the longitude is ٮح ل, with a line over the numerals (note a).
L04: the manuscript lacks the word طول, which the editor supplies (note b).
L04: a variant reading of the latitude is مه ل, with a line over the numerals (note c).
L06: a variant reading of the second longitude is ٮح ك, with a line over the numerals (note d).
L07: the manuscript has a gap at the minutes of the longitude; the editor supplies them from S (note e).
L07: a variant reading of the second latitude is مح م, with a line over the numerals (note f).
L08: a variant reading of the first longitude is ٮح ل, with a line over the numerals (note g).
L11: a variant reading of the first longitude is كه ه, with a line over the numerals (note h).
L12: a variant reading of the first latitude is ند ح (note i).
observations: The running text of the outer western and northern sea goes on from p. 67 (frame 073): the coast from point to point, with the degrees and the minutes of each longitude and latitude written with letters under one line, transcribed with {ov:…}, the editor's running numbers in parentheses, (١٠٠٣)-(١٠٢٧), and the numbers of Suhrāb in square brackets, [٥٨٧]-[٦١٠]; point 1014 (L08) has none. L01: «وهناك مصبّ نهر», there is the mouth of a river, without its name; L05-L06: «على صورة القوارة», along the shape of the qawwāra; L13: «ويرجع الى», it returns to; L16: «على صورة الطيلسان», along the shape of the ṭaylasān. «يمرّ», «ويمرّ», «ثمّ» and «مصبّ» are printed with a shadda.

L05: the folio of the Strasbourg manuscript, «(fol. 17ᵃ)», is printed in Latin type within the line, between «والعرض» and the latitude «مو كه», not in the margin; transcribed as a margin note before the line.

L04: the word «طول» is printed between angle brackets, «⟨طول⟩», followed by the note mark b: the editor supplies it, which the manuscript lacks (note b). L07: the minutes of the longitude are the sign for zero between angle brackets, followed by the note mark e: the editor supplies them from S where the manuscript has a gap (note e).

Note marks: L03, a after the longitude; L04, b after «⟨طول⟩» and c after the latitude; L06, d after the second longitude; L07, e after the longitude and f after the second latitude; L08, g after the first longitude; L11, h after the first longitude; L12, i after the first latitude.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: a tooth without its dot in the degrees of the longitude, ٮح (L02, L04, L05, L06, L08), ٮد (L03), ٮو (L03, L09) and ٮط (L07, L08), which read with a ي give 18, 14, 16 and 19, and in the degrees of the latitude, ٮح (L13, L14), which read as a ن gives 58, beside the latitudes 61° 30′ before them and 58° 40′ (L15) after; مٮ (L14, the degrees of the longitude), a م joined to a final ب without its dot, 42; ٮه (L01, L05, the minutes of the longitude; L06, L08, L10, L13, the minutes of the latitude), a tooth joined to a final ه, the form that L11 prints with the dot of the ن, نه. L03: above the tooth of ٮد stands a speck, 4 by 4 px, much smaller than the dots of the font, about 9 by 9 px. With their dots: ير (L06), with the two dots of the ي; يه (L10); ند (L12), with the dot of the ن touching the top of its tooth; نا (L10, L15), نه (L11), نح (L15), نو (L15), نط (L15), ن (L06, L10).

In these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed: ر (L02, the degrees of the first longitude), ير (L06, the degrees of the longitude), 17, and مر (L06, the degrees of the latitude), 47.

The ح of the numerals, ٮح (L02, L04-L06, L08, L13, L14), مح (L07, L08, the latitudes; L13, the longitude) and نح (L15), shows no dot in the bowl; the same form is a ج without its dot, 3. Transcribed as printed.

L13, the degrees of the first longitude, «مح»: the م is printed broken, its loop, 12 by 18 px, and a blot of 13 by 15 px standing apart at the top of the ح. Transcribed مح. L16: the longitude «سو ل» is printed faintly and broken in places.
The isolated ك, 20, is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter (L03, L09, L10). The isolated ى, 10, has no dots (L15).

Marks not transcribed: L03, a small curled mark, 16 by 13 px, below the last digit of [٥٩٠]; in the footnotes, a scribble drawn by hand in pencil over the Arabic form of note i, not part of the print.
The editor's footnotes stand in three lines below a short rule at the left: notes a-i. The page number «— ٦٨ —» stands at the foot, centred.
